cases.input: What does temperature do in LLM sampling?
cases.expected: Temperature controls randomness. Lower values make output more deterministic; higher values make it more creative/varied.

cases.input: What is the difference between fine-tuning and prompting?
cases.expected: Prompting steers the model at inference time with instructions. Fine-tuning updates the model weights on new data, changing behaviour permanently.

cases.input: What is an eval and why does it matter?
cases.expected: An eval is a repeatable test suite that measures model output quality. It matters because it catches regressions and gives an honest performance signal.

cases.input: Explain prompt injection in one sentence.

cases.input: What is the difference between a hosted model and a local model?
cases.expected: Hosted models run on a provider's servers (e.g. Gemini, GPT-4) — easy to use but cost money and send data externally. Local models (e.g. Ollama) run on your own hardware — private and free but slower without a GPU.
